tell: A xanthine oxidase inhibitor whose boxed warning concerns cardiovascular death compared with allopurinol.

clues.text: Absolute bioavailability has not been studied, and it may be taken without regard to food. Plasma protein binding is 99.2%, mainly to albumin, and elimination is both hepatic and renal.
A non-hygroscopic crystalline powder with a molecular weight of 316.38 that is practically insoluble in water.
Approved under an NDA as 40 mg and 80 mg tablets, dosed once daily.

Boxed warning for a higher rate of cardiovascular death than with the comparator drug in an outcomes study of patients with established cardiovascular disease. Contraindicated with azathioprine or mercaptopurine.

Chronic management of hyperuricemia in adult patients with an inadequate response to a maximally titrated dose of allopurinol, intolerance to it, or where it is not advisable; not for asymptomatic hyperuricemia.
Acts as a xanthine oxidase inhibitor, lowering serum uric acid, and is not expected to inhibit other enzymes of purine and pyrimidine synthesis at therapeutic concentrations.
The generic name begins with F and has ten letters.
